claims.claimTextOrPointer: Item 1.01 (verbatim): "On August 17, 2026, NVIDIA entered into multiple residual value guaranties (collectively, the “Agreements”) with SB Energy (the “Lessor”) relating to leases for approximately 4.25 gigawatts of IT load in the aggregate at the Portsmouth Site." and "NVIDIA’s aggregate payment obligation is cumulatively capped at $105 billion for its initial commitment under the Agreements."
Exhibit 99.1 press release announcing the SB Energy partnership, furnished under Item 7.01 Regulation FD.
claims._note: Same filer and same accession as claim-b-001. It corroborates but is NOT an independent source.

reasoning: claim-b-001 is an OFFICIAL SEC filing whose exact bytes are sha256-pinned in this repository, so it satisfies the official-evidence path once the existing parse-agreement and bonded-publication checks pass.
The event is materially discontinuous: a newly disclosed direct financial obligation capped at $105 billion, against roughly 4.25 GW of IT load.
It landed while the US reference market was closed, which is precisely the asymmetry Tinjau claims to guard.
PROTECT still requires an independent market consequence. Evidence alone does not authorise the bounded action.

_schemaChangeLog: 0.2.0 (T1.2): added `materiality` to every claim. T1.1 made materiality a separate axis from provenance, because an official filing is not automatically an LP-relevant corporate action. The engine treats a missing value as UNKNOWN and refuses to promote on it, so the field had to be stated rather than inferred.
